from_quote: I have just met with your performance in favour of the Honourable Mr. Gerry, published in the Maryland Journal of the i8th January, 1788.
rationale: The letter is addressed to Luther Martin and answers his defence of Mr. Gerry, which it dates to the Maryland Journal of 18 January 1788 (printed "i8th" in the OCR), the date of this letter of Martin's.

from_quote: never heard Mr. Gerry, or any other member, introduce a proposition for the redemption of Continental money according to its nominal or any other value
rationale: Quotes, as "You have said," Martin's statement that he never heard Mr. Gerry or any other member propose the redemption of continental money.
to_quote: never heard Mr. Gerry or any other member introduce a proposition for the redemption of continental money according to its nominal or any other value

from_quote: This Constitution and the laws of the United States which shall be made in pursuance thereof, and all treaties made or which shall be made, under the authority of the United States, shall be the supreme law of the land, and the judges in every State shall be bound thereby, anything in the Constitution or the law of any State to the contrary notwithstanding.
rationale: Quotes this clause in full in quotation marks, introducing it as "that clause in the Constitution which enacts."
to_quote: This Constitution, and the Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof; and all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding.

from_quote: the clause that declares nine States to be sufficient to put the government in motion
rationale: Names "the clause that declares nine States to be sufficient to put the government in motion"; this is the only clause that sets the number of ratifying states.
to_quote: The Ratification of the Conventions of nine States, shall be sufficient
